questions.prompt: Where must parameters with default values go in the def line?
choices: They must be the only parameters
questions.explain: Python matches arguments to parameters left to right. If a defaulted parameter came first there would be no way to tell which one an unlabelled argument was meant for, so it is a syntax error.

questions.prompt: With def greet(name, greeting="Hello"):, what does greet("Ada") print?
questions.explain: The missing argument falls back to the default written in the def line, so greeting is "Hello" for that call.

questions.prompt: With def order(item, quantity=1, gift=False):, which calls are valid?
questions.explain: Only item is required. A keyword argument can skip over a defaulted parameter, which is why the third call works without mentioning quantity. The last call leaves out the one argument that has no default.

questions.prompt: A parameter is made optional by giving it a ___ value in the def line.
questions.explain: The value written after the equals sign in the def line is the default, used whenever the caller does not supply one.
